Easy Homemade Hummus From Dried Chickpeas (Instant Pot)

Instant pot cooked chickpeas blended with simple clean ingredients like bright fresh lemon, savory garlic, nutty tahini, warm cumin, and just a touch of smoky paprika to make smooth and creamy homemade hummus.

By Rachel Maser

This is the best hummus recipe to make with dried chickpeas because it’s just soo easy!  We use an Instant pot for super fast cooking, then blend the cooked chickpeas with simple clean ingredients like bright fresh lemon, savory garlic, nutty tahini, warm cumin, and just a touch of smoky paprika to make smooth and creamy homemade hummus that’s way better than store-bought!

Creamy Homemade Hummus From Dried Chickpeas

Once you make hummus from scratch, it’s hard to return to store-bought hummus! This Instant Pot Hummus is incredibly smooth and creamy, made with lemon juice, tahini, garlic, and salt, plus a bit of warm cumin and smoky paprika. 

Cooking dried chickpeas until extra tender gives the best hummus texture…without peeling each individual chickpea. Plus, it’s BUDGET FRIENDLY!

Why You’ll Love This Recipe

Creamy, flavorful, and full of fiber! This homemade Instant Pot Hummus proves that a simple bowl of dried chickpeas can become seriously crave-worthy.  Here are a few more reasons you’ll love this easy recipe:

  • Instant Pot Recipe:  The pressure cooker makes preparing dried chickpeas mostly hands-off. One batch makes enough for two batches of hummus; or plenty of extra chickpeas to roast for snacking.
  • Simple Recipe:  Simple flavors like lemon, salt, cumin, and paprika make this the perfect universal dip for snacking and dipping vegetables.
  • Clean Ingredients:   Clean ingredients are used in this homemade hummus recipe, unlike what you may find if you look at the ingredients on a grocery store brand.
  • Budget Friendly:  Whether using canned or dried garbanzo beans, they are both a super inexpensive way to get protein and fiber into your diet.

Looking for a few different flavors of hummus to try? Then you may love our easy dill pickle hummus or our spicy jalapeno and avocado hummus.

Health Benefits of Homemade Hummus

Chickpeas are naturally packed with fiber and a bit of plant-based protein, making this a satisfying dip, snack, or addition to a meal. Fiber helps support healthy digestion and keeps meals feeling more substantial, while tahini and extra-virgin olive oil add richness and nourishing fats. Plus, hummus is a gluten free and dairy free snack.

Ingredients

These are the simple ingredients that make this homemade hummus recipe perfect for healthy snacking and dipping.

Chickpeas: Also known as garbanzo beans, chickpeas lend mostly fiber to this recipe to help keep you full.  We used dried chickpeas and cooked them until past tender, and almost mushy, in the instant pot. 

Tahini:  Tahini is a paste made from sesame seeds and helps turn the blended chickpeas into creamy hummus while also adding nutty flavor. 

Lemon:  Fresh lemon juice is added for brightness. 

Garlic:  Garlic is a traditional flavor in hummus.

Salt:  To bring out the other flavors in the homemade hummus.

Cumin:  To give our hummus recipe a bit of warmth.

Paprika:  For a little bit of smokey flavor.

Olive Oil:  Always choose a high-quality extra virgin olive oil, never canola or another type of oil, for your hummus. Here is an olive oil I like.

See the recipe card for full information on all ingredients and quantities.

Variations And Substitutions

  • Use Canned Chickpeas:  You can absolutely use canned chickpeas (garbanzo beans) in this recipe to make it faster.  Chickpeas straight from the can can create a grainy hummus unless you cook the canned chickpeas in boiling water first, until they are very soft.  That also makes the canned chickpeas warm so they incorporate with the other ingredients more easily.
  • Different Flavors:  Use the flavors and spices you like.  Create an Italian hummus using oregano and basil, a Mexican hummus with chipotle chili’s, cumin, and cilantro, or a Greek roasted garlic hummus.
  • Alternate Cooking Methods:  You can also cook your dried chickpeas in a stockpot on the stove or in a slow cooker.  This will change the cooking time. 

How To Make Homemade Hummus From Dried Chickpeas

Step 1. Rinse and sort the dried chickpeas, discarding any debris.

Step 2. Add the chickpeas, 6–7 cups water, and bay leaf to a 6-quart Instant Pot. Make sure the contents remain below the pot’s halfway line.

Secure the lid and cook on High Pressure for 40 minutes. Allow the pressure to release naturally until the float valve drops. Carefully remove the lid and test a chickpea; it should crush effortlessly between your fingers. If the chickpeas are still firm, cook for an additional 5–10 minutes.

Discard the bay leaf. Reserve at least 1 cup of cooking liquid, then drain the chickpeas. Measure 3 cups for the hummus. Refrigerate or freeze the remaining chickpeas for another batch.

Step 3. Add the tahini and lemon juice to a food processor and blend for about 1 minute, scraping down the bowl as needed. Add the garlic, sea salt, cumin, smoked paprika, and ¼ cup cooking liquid; blend until smooth and creamy.

Step 4. Add 3 cups of warm cooked chickpeas and process for 2–3 minutes. For an extra-light, smooth texture, add 1–2 ice cubes while the processor is running. Slowly stream in the olive oil.

Step 5. Add more reserved cooking liquid, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the hummus reaches your preferred consistency. Taste and adjust the lemon juice and sea salt.

Step 6. Transfer to a serving bowl and finish with a very small drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, roasted chickpeas, chopped parsley, cumin, or smoked paprika.

Rachel’s Tips For The Best Results

  • For the creamiest hummus, use very soft chickpeas. They should look slightly overcooked rather than just tender.
  • Blend longer than you think. Two to three uninterrupted minutes helps create a noticeably smooth hummus texture.
  • Taste after blending. Chickpeas can mute seasoning, so the hummus may need another pinch of salt or squeeze of lemon.
  • Adjust the tahini if desired. Your ¼ cup creates a mild sesame flavor. Readers who prefer richer, more traditional-tasting hummus can increase it to ⅓ or ½ cup.
  • Smoked paprika changes the flavor. Keep it if you want smoky hummus. For a more classic version, use regular paprika as a garnish instead.
  • If the hummus is too thick, add more reserved cooking liquid, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the hummus reaches your preferred consistency.
  • The secret for fluffy texture is to add ice cubes or ice water to the food processor while blending.

One pound of dried chickpeas yields approximately 6 cups cooked which is enough for two batches of this hummus. You can also use the extra cooked chickpeas to make our Roasted BBQ Chickpeas.

How To Serve Homemade Hummus

Serve this hummus with plenty of crunchy vegetables like cucumbers or celery, warm pita bread, pita chips, crackers, or spread it onto wraps and sandwiches for an easy boost of flavor and nutrition.  These are some of the recipes where we use hummus:

  • Hummus Cucumber Roll-Ups make the perfect clean eats appetizer for your next get together.
  • A fresh hummus salad bowl adds flavor, a little protein, and a lot of fiber to your normal lettuce salad.
  • This Mediterranean Bowl adds hummus as a creamy, flavorful extra in this meal prep bowl.

Make Ahead and Storage Tips

Make this hummus ahead of time and store it in the refrigerator or freezer.  Freeze it in small portions so you can pull one out and use it for a week. 

  • Refrigerate for up to 4 days in an airtight container.
  • Freeze for up to 2 months in an airtight container.
  • Thaw in the fridge overnight.

Recipe FAQs

Does hummus need to be refrigerated?

Yes, you should refrigerate hummus unless you are going to eat it right away.

Does hummus have fiber?

Yes, this easy homemade hummus recipe made with dried chickpeas has a total of 32 grams of fiber or 1 gram per serving.

Can you freeze hummus?

Hummus freezes really well for up to 2 months in an airtight container.

Do I have to soak chickpeas before cooking?

It is not necessary to soak your dry chickpeas before cooking when using this instant pot hummus recipe.

Homemade Hummus With Dried Chickpeas (Instant Pot)

Instant pot cooked chickpeas blended with simple clean ingredients like bright fresh lemon, savory garlic, nutty tahini, warm cumin, and just a touch of smoky paprika to make smooth and creamy homemade hummus.
Prep: 5 minutes mins
Cook: 40 minutes mins
Total: 45 minutes mins

Equipment

  • Vegetable Peeler
  • Best Chef’s Knife
  • Non-Toxic Acacia Wood Cutting Board
  • Instant Pot Duo

Ingredients 

For the Instant Pot chickpeas:

  • 1 lb. dried chickpeas, rinsed and sorted
  • 6 –7 cups water
  • 1 bay leaf

For the Hummus:

  • 3 cups cooked garbanzo beans
  • 1/4 cup tahini
  • 1/4 cup freshly squeezed lemon juice
  • 2 fresh garlic cloves
  • 1 tsp sea salt
  • 1/2 tsp ground cumin , plus more for garnish
  • 1/2 tsp smoked paprika , plus more for garnish
  • ¼ – ½ cup reserved cooking liquid, start with less
  • 2 Tbsps high-quality extra virgin olive oil , plus more for serving
US Customary – Metric

Instructions 

To cook your garbanzo beans/chickpeas in an Instant Pot:

  • Rinse and sort the dried chickpeas, discarding any debris. Add the chickpeas, 6–7 cups water, and bay leaf to a 6-quart Instant Pot. Make sure the contents remain below the pot’s halfway line.
  • Secure the lid and cook on High Pressure for 40 minutes. Allow the pressure to release naturally until the float valve drops. Carefully remove the lid and test a chickpea; it should crush effortlessly between your fingers. If the chickpeas are still firm, cook for an additional 5–10 minutes.
  • Discard the bay leaf. Reserve at least 1 cup of cooking liquid, then drain the chickpeas. Measure 3 cups for the hummus. Refrigerate or freeze the remaining chickpeas for another batch.
  • One pound of dried chickpeas yields approximately 6 cups cooked—enough for two batches of this hummus. You can also use the extras to make our Roasted BBQ Chickpeas

To make the hummus:

  • Add the tahini and lemon juice to a food processor and blend for about 1 minute, scraping down the bowl as needed. Add the garlic, sea salt, cumin, smoked paprika, and ¼ cup cooking liquid; blend until smooth and creamy.
  • Add 3 cups of warm cooked chickpeas and process for 2–3 minutes. For an extra-light, smooth texture, add 1–2 ice cubes while the processor is running. Slowly stream in the olive oil. Add more reserved cooking liquid, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the hummus reaches your preferred consistency. Taste and adjust the lemon juice and sea salt.
  • Transfer to a serving bowl and finish with a very small drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, roasted chickpeas, chopped parsley, cumin, or smoked paprika.
  • Serve with your favorite vegetables.

Notes

  • For the creamiest hummus, use very soft chickpeas. They should look slightly overcooked rather than just tender.
  • Blend longer than you think. Two to three uninterrupted minutes helps create a noticeably smooth hummus texture.
  • Taste after blending. Chickpeas can mute seasoning, so the hummus may need another pinch of salt or squeeze of lemon.
  • Adjust the tahini if desired. Your ¼ cup creates a mild sesame flavor. Readers who prefer richer, more traditional-tasting hummus can increase it to ⅓ or ½ cup.
  • Smoked paprika changes the flavor. Keep it if you want smoky hummus. For a more classic version, use regular paprika as a garnish instead.
  • If the hummus is too thick, add more reserved cooking liquid, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the hummus reaches your preferred consistency.
  • The secret for fluffy texture is to add ice cubes or ice water to the food processor while blending.
 

Make Ahead and Storage Tips

Make this hummus ahead of time and store it in the refrigerator or freezer.  Freeze it in small portions so you can pull one out and use it for a week. 
  • Refrigerate for up to 4 days in an airtight container.
  • Freeze for up to 2 months in an airtight container.
  • Thaw in the fridge overnight.
